title: AA Batteries 8-pack

drivers.name: Thanksgiving (holiday)
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted historical effect x1.0; only 2 past occurrences, weak signal.

drivers.name: 10% off promotion
drivers.evidence: Noise-adjusted lift x1.17 from 7 past promotions; this is a smaller discount than prior 15-30% events.

drivers.name: Store closed Monday
drivers.evidence: Store closure on first day of week; 1/7 of weekly sales lost; no prior data on closure impact, but plausible.

adjustment.analysis: Thanksgiving drives demand, but noise-adjusted historical effect is x1.0—no reliable uplift. The 10% discount is smaller than past promotions (15-30% off) and has a noise-adjusted lift of x1.17. Store closure on Monday reduces sales by ~15% (1/7 of week). The classical model's 1.17 is too high: it doesn't account for the store closure or the weak event signal. Shrink lift toward 1.0 due to limited evidence and price depth. No pantry-loading effect expected as this is not a high-velocity promo.

  planner notes: Store closed Monday for renovation

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 34.8 | 5%-95%: 17.9 - 58.9 | 10%-90%: 20.3 - 55.7

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-44% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
